blocks.text: DARWIN — Growers in Australia’s mango heartlands are warning that the fruits of their labor are at risk if federal changes to working holiday visas go ahead. The Northern Territory (NT) government says the changes will leave the Top End mango harvest short of 1,000 workers, with 70 percent of the crop left to rot on the trees. Growers, meanwhile, warn that fruit left on the trees would mean fewer mangoes making it to market, leading to higher prices for consumers.
